comments.text: Little extra on the tick bite question, not ALL ticks carry Lyme disease. Here in Belgium, as a vet, I can send all the ticks you get of your cat or dog to a lab to have those analysed to see IF they carried any tick borne diseases. Because there are a few other diseases than Lyme disease that ticks can transfer. Lyme disease is just the most commonly known one. We use the same ab for when we think the chance of Lyme disease is high in cats and dogs.

comments.text: Re: tick bites and Lyme disease. I would also add that not all tick species carry the disease. Among those that are vectors (the Blacklegged Tick/Deer Tick and Western Blacklegged Tick), only about 20-50% are carriers depending on the region. Other tick species carry different diseases so if you find a tick attached to you, it's important to ID it and look up the diseases common in your area. You can also put them in a Ziploc bag and freeze them to have it tested by a lab should you later get sick (or for peace of mind but the testing can be expensive).
